meta.title: Fliks: your personal video collection, on every screen
meta.description: Fliks is a self-hosted media server and streaming app for your own video collection. Free, open source, AGPL-3.0.

hero.title: Your personal video collection, on every screen in the house.
hero.subtitle: Point Fliks at the folders where your films and shows live. It handles the rest: covers, synopses, cast, seasons and episodes, laid out like the apps you already use. This library is entirely yours.
hero.imageAlt: The home page, a library, discovery and a film page

features.title: Everything a streaming night needs
features.subtitle: A full streaming service for the whole household, running on hardware you already own.

items.title: Subtitles found for you
items.text: A video with none? Fliks searches the usual subtitle sites and picks the one that matches your copy.

items.title: Translated by AI
items.text: No track in your language? Translate one you have with Gemini, any OpenAI-compatible model or LibreTranslate. Saved next to the video, done once.

items.title: Out of sync, fixed in one click
items.text: Fliks listens to the dialogue and slides the subtitles back onto it. No hunting for the right offset.

items.title: Image subtitles made readable
items.text: DVD and Blu-ray picture subtitles are read by OCR and turned into text you can restyle and translate.

items.title: HDR on any screen
items.text: HDR10, HLG and Dolby Vision are tone-mapped to SDR when the screen cannot show them, so the picture never looks washed out.

items.title: Live TV you can pause
items.text: Bring your IPTV playlist: a program guide next to your library, with pause and rewind on live channels.

items.title: Ads skipped, cuts honoured
items.text: Drop the .edl file Comskip or MCEBuddy can write next to a video: Fliks skips the commercials, jumps the cuts and mutes what should be muted.

items.title: Spoiler protection
items.text: Blurs the synopsis and thumbnail of anything you have not watched yet, and hides episode titles that give the plot away.

items.title: Suggestions from what you watch
items.text: Recommendations weighted by what you actually watched, not by what is trending.

items.title: Release calendar
items.text: Upcoming episodes and releases for what you follow, on one calendar.

items.title: Rich metadata
items.text: Posters, cast and crew. Every person gets a page listing their work in your libraries.

items.title: Remote control
items.text: Pick another device from your phone and play there. Pause, seek, switch subtitles or quality from the couch, between any two Fliks apps.

items.title: Quick Connect for TVs
items.text: Pick your profile on the TV, approve it from your phone. No password to type with a remote.

items.title: Recommend something to someone
items.text: Send a film or a season to another user. It shows up on their home page with your name on it.

items.title: Shared playlists
items.text: Invite other users as viewer, editor or admin and build one together.

items.title: Downloads that keep themselves current
items.text: Download a whole season or show in one tap. Set a series or playlist to automatic: the next episodes stay on the device and watched ones are removed. Wifi-only and a storage cap keep it in check.

items.title: Watch parties
items.text: Press play together: synced playback, chat and voice. Add films to the programme, vote on what to watch, or open a public party. Web, mobile, desktop and Apple TV, with TVs following along.

items.title: Hardware transcoding
items.text: Intel QSV, VAAPI, NVIDIA NVENC, AMD AMF and Apple VideoToolbox, detected at startup, with a CPU fallback.

items.title: Live transcode dashboard
items.text: Who is watching what, at which quality, on which hardware path, and why a transcode was needed.

items.title: Why is it stuttering?
items.text: Every app reports how each playback went. Fliks tells you whether the network, the device or the server was to blame, with a timeline of every freeze.

items.title: Requests with auto-approval
items.text: Household members ask for titles; rules you set approve the ones you trust.

items.title: Cleanup with a countdown
items.text: Rules flag stale titles by age, play history or play count. They wait in a leaving-soon list, with reminders before anything is removed.

items.title: Signed, isolated plugins
items.text: Add what you need from the plugin catalog. Archives are signed, and plugin code runs in its own process.

platforms.title: Everywhere you watch
platforms.subtitle: Start a film on your phone and finish it on the TV. Your place follows you.
platforms.serverList: Docker, a Windows tray app, a macOS menu-bar app, or from source.
platforms.clientList: Web, iOS, Android, Android TV, Apple TV, Samsung TV, LG TV, desktop, Chromecast, Nintendo Switch.

getStarted.title: Get started in 2 minutes
getStarted.subtitle: All you need is a folder with your videos.
getStarted.dockerStep2: Set your media path and passwords, then start it
getStarted.otherWays: Windows and macOS installers are on the releases page. Linux is on APT and the Snap Store.

why.title: Why self-hosted
why.subtitle: The library is yours, and so is the machine it runs on.

items.title: Your data stays home
items.text: No account to create, no subscription, nothing leaves the house.

items.title: Free and open source
items.text: AGPL-3.0-or-later. Read the code, change it, run a modified version.

items.title: No catalog to lose
items.text: Your files, your metadata, your history. Nothing disappears because a license expired.

items.title: Runs on what you have
items.text: A NAS, a spare machine, a home server. Hardware transcoding when the machine offers it.

community.title: Open source, built in the open
community.subtitle: Every change, every release and every discussion happens on GitHub.

download.metaDescription: Install the Fliks server with Docker, on Windows, macOS or TrueNAS, then get the apps for desktop, iOS, Android, Apple TV, Android TV, LG and Samsung TVs.
download.title: Fliks on every screen
download.subtitle: Install the server once, on the machine that holds your media, then watch from any screen with the same account.

server.title: Install the server
server.subtitle: It scans your media, streams it and keeps every account in sync.

docker.label: Docker
docker.text: The recommended way. Download the example Compose file, set the database passwords and your media folder, then start it and open http://<host>:4848.
docker.meta: linux/amd64, linux/arm64 · Intel QSV, VAAPI, NVIDIA NVENC

windows.label: Windows
windows.text: A tray app that bundles PostgreSQL, FFmpeg and the server: nothing else to install, no administrator prompt.
windows.meta: Windows 10 or 11, x64 · Intel QSV, AMD AMF, NVIDIA NVENC, auto-detected

macos.label: macOS
macos.text: A menu-bar app that bundles everything it needs. Signed and notarized, it updates itself.
macos.meta: macOS 13 or later, Apple Silicon · VideoToolbox

truenas.label: TrueNAS
truenas.text: In Apps > Discover Apps, enable the Community train and install fliks. Set a database password and add your media under Additional Storage.
truenas.meta: TrueNAS SCALE · web UI on port 30485

source.label: From source
source.text: Build the Rust server and the web client yourself. You provide PostgreSQL and FFmpeg.
source.meta: Any platform Rust targets · whatever your FFmpeg exposes

clients.title: Watch on your screens
clients.subtitle: Every app connects to your server: enter its address, sign in, and your library, progress and preferences follow you.

computer.title: Computer
computer.details: On Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13 or later, add the Fliks repository and install the app with APT. Or run sudo snap install fliks. The desktop app plays through mpv, so it Direct Plays more formats than a browser.

mobile.title: Phone and tablet
mobile.details: Both apps save titles for offline viewing and download in the background. The .apk is the same Android app, for devices without Google Play.

tv.title: TV
tv.details: Choose Quick Connect: the TV shows a code you type on your phone, under Login requests. Fliks is not on Samsung Apps yet: the .wgt is sideloaded with Tizen Studio, see the Samsung guide.

other.title: Nothing to install
other.details: Open your server's address in a browser and sign in. Its Install option adds Fliks to your home screen or desktop, in its own window. Chromecast is a cast target from any app.

web.name: Web browser
web.min: Any current browser, at your server's address

download.encodersSubtitle: Which hardware path is available depends on the machine, not on Fliks. It probes at startup and falls back to CPU when nothing else answers.
download.encodersNote: HDR10, HLG and Dolby Vision are tone-mapped to SDR when the receiving device cannot render them.
